title: CI/CD Tutorial using GitHub Actions - Automated Testing & Automated Deployments

cues.text: nine out of 10 people hate this
developer the one that doesn't automate
anything and if you're watching this the
likelihood is that you're that developer
so how can you automate your deployment
so that you never have to deal with
another deployment error ever again cicd

the manual tasks that us M Mortals

our code to production things like
compiling our code or running tests or
uploading our code to our Cloud
infrastructure automating things not

removes the possibility of human error

the ground there are a bunch of tools
out there that can help you get started
with cicd and I've used a few of them
all of them are great at what they do
however in this video we're going to be
focusing specifically on GitHub actions
let's get started ultimately all you
need to get started is a GitHub

video at the top of your repository page

running we can see the progress of each

deploy it to our production server

do it ourselves or every time we create
a new pull request we might want to test

two examples that we're going to build
today there's a huge list of different

because this workflow is going to be

most common one that people will use

do it manually through the command line
using a buntu it just saves a bit of
time the first step is going to be
adding our code to our virtual
environments using the checkout action
now I want you to have a think about the
steps that you would take if you were
testing your code manually firstly you
want to make sure that all of your
dependencies have been install for your
project we can do this by running mpmi
which is going to run a clean install
once your dependencies have been stalled
you can run your tests using whatever
Library you're using in your project I
